title: Moon base: fourteen days of night (continuous takes, hidden joins)
note: Nov 23-24. Six shots, no plain cut. Shots 1 and 5 are continuous camera moves across NASA's 4K concept animation 'Living and Working on the Moon' (May 2026): night_fall.py makes one wide picture of the whole base (specs/night_v10_take1.json, night_v10_take2.json) with our shadow, night, lamps, beacons, stars and spacecraft lights, and pan_window.py moves a 1080x1920 frame across it at 1:1. Shot 2 is from NASA's 'Moon Base: Rovers and Lunar Terrain Vehicles' (Oct 2026); shots 3, 4 and 6 from the animated parts of NASA's November 2026 Moon Base update; each a 9:16 window of the 4K frame scaled down and graded toward our night. The joins are made by seam.py. Stars are real (HYG catalogue), placed for a view along the ecliptic from the south pole with the Sun at ecliptic longitude 292 degrees (mid-January); the source gives no date, so the date is our assumption. Credit NASA. Sound effects are synthesised (sfx.py).

shots.job: This shot starts on the Sun low over a ridge and follows a lander's engine light and the ridge's shadow across the base, as its lamps come on and the stars come out, so the viewer sees the night arrive over the whole base. (NASA concept animation; shadow, night, lamps, beacons, stars and spacecraft lights added)
This shot shows two astronauts at a rover in the dark, lit by their helmet lamps, so the viewer sees the people who cannot be switched off. (NASA, Rovers video, 0:14)
This shot shows a power mast standing over a lit unit in the dark, so the viewer sees what has to keep running. (NASA, November update)
This shot shows tall solar masts standing in the dark until their panels catch the first sunlight, so the viewer sees the night end where the base reaches highest. (NASA, November update)

This shot shows sunlight catching the high ridge under a crescent Earth and crossing the plain, then turns across the base to where the shadow is already coming back and the lamps come on again, so the viewer sees that the light at the pole is long but does not last. (NASA concept animation; night, light, lamps, beacons and stars added)
This shot shows an astronaut close, helmet lamps on, checking a wrist display in the dark, so the viewer sees the person the promise is about. (NASA, November update)

lines.say: On most of the Moon, night lasts about fourteen days.
Small landers have survived it by mostly shutting down.
No base with people has yet run through a lunar night.
